trust_decision.summary: Per-placeholder denylist checks decide whether an untrusted lng/ns value may be put into the loadPath/addPath template that becomes the request URL; interpolateUrl returns null to refuse the request, and _readAny/create skip it.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'incomplete URL validation'. The shared denylist regex in isSafeUrlSegmentBase is the obvious validator to look at, and the fix tightens it there.

fix_sites.entry_point: Backend.read / readMulti / create (and reload via backendConnector.read) -> interpolateUrl; also exported helpers isSafeLangUrlSegment/isSafeNsUrlSegment
Backend.read / readMulti / create -> interpolateUrl -> isSafeNsUrlSegment for the {{ns}} placeholder
Same API, through the browser IIFE bundle (global i18nextHttpBackend)
fix_sites.module_kind: committed build artifact (second copy of lib/utils.js)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The committed bundles i18nextHttpBackend.js:11-28 and i18nextHttpBackend.min.js are built from lib/utils.js, not a separate implementation

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A template with a leading literal '/' followed directly by {{ns}} (e.g. '/{{ns}}/{{lng}}.json') looks like a 'template with a leading path', which the fix's own changelog declares unaffected (fix.diff:10). Also, ns legitimately allows '/' (lib/utils.js:52-57), so a solver can argue that a single leading slash is a valid nested-namespace shape.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: ns must keep accepting '/' (nested namespaces like a/b) and '@' (scoped names like @org/pkg), regressions fixed in 3.0.6/4.0.1. Blocking '/' or '@' in ns, or rejecting every URL that is absolute or starts with a protocol, breaks legitimate behaviour: loadPath may legitimately be an absolute cross-origin URL such as https://cdn/... {{lng}}.

O6_input_shapes: '+'-joined multi-language value with one bad segment (en+http:...), via split at lib/utils.js:155-161

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The composed URL is never checked. An ns with a single leading '/' passes the per-value check but, placed after a literal '/' in the template (e.g. '/{{ns}}/{{lng}}.json'), it yields a protocol-relative '//host/...' URL that leaves the origin.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The template has a leading '/', which the changelog calls unaffected, and a leading '/' in ns is a legitimate nested-namespace character.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file and function as the landing point; the gap is in template/value composition, not in the denylist

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Public Backend.loadUrl(url, ...) sends a caller-supplied URL to options.request with no URL check.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The caller passes a complete URL, not lng/ns values, so there is nothing to interpolate. It is arguably outside the placeholder-injection protection.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other file (lib/index.js) from the landing point; public in index.d.ts:126-131

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A function-form loadPath gets the raw languages/namespaces and could return a pre-interpolated string that skips interpolateUrl.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer could add a 'pre-built path' fast path for function loadPath results that contain no placeholders.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The unchecked 'interpolate' helper could be used for addPath or a new path option (e.g. a reload or customPath variant).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: interpolate already exists next to interpolateUrl, and a new option could easily reach for the wrong one.

O9_family: URL/SSRF injection via template interpolation (CWE-918/CWE-74), validated by an incomplete denylist
